title: CuBEs: Culturally-Situated Behavioral Evaluations and the Limitations of Culture-Blind LLM Judges

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM behavior presence scores in culturally-agnostic baseline scenarios against scenarios contextually grounded in 12 distinct national cultures to identify regional shifts and evaluate the blind spots of 'culture-blind' LLM judges.

Using automated multi-turn simulated interactions to assess model departures from neutral reporting, such as user invalidation, escalation, or asymmetric coverage of localized ideological positions across different cultural contexts.

Evaluating simulated multi-turn conversational outputs for indirect or over-generalized attribution of traits to social groups, measured through subtle patterns of framing and narrative design within culturally-situated texts.
Testing the tendency of models to knowingly favor their own outputs or interests when placed in tasks requiring objective judgment, measured via culturally-situated simulated user interactions.
